pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education Curriculum | St. Peter's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education Curriculum
At St. Peter’s we follow the RED (Religious Education Directory) throughout the whole school, using the “Day by Day” resources in line with the Diocesan guidance. The 6-branch structure of the RED closely follows the liturgical year and allows pupils to deepen their understanding of Christ and the Catholic faith.
In addition to this, our curriculum allows children the opportunity to encounter other Christian beliefs and the beliefs and practices of other world faiths with an attitude of respect and tolerance. Through each branch we follow and learn more about the life of Jesus through scripture, helping children to understand, discern and respond to the word of God.
The six branches are as followed:
Autumn 1: Creation and Covenant
Autmn 2: Prophecy and Promise
Spring 1: Galilee to Jerusalem
Spring 2: Desert to Garden
Summer 2: Dialogue and Encounter

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Reading | St. Peter's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Reading
In Early Years, developing the skills of early reading is a priority. We encourage reading throughout the day and continue to enhance the child’s journey with reading at home. To inspire a love of reading amongst the children, we encourage parents/carers to read with their child regularly and provide them with books to share. At school, we have wide range of quality texts that are promoted throughout the learning environment both inside and outside. Children enjoy the opportunities to share, listen, act out, re-tell and read books daily. Book corners are stimulating and accessible, owned and loved by children. Class teachers also carefully choose texts to read to their classes every day.
Pupils who are at the early stages of their phonics development are given a decodable text so that they can practice what they have learnt. The decodable text will focus on recently and previously learnt sounds (not the current focus of learning for that week) so that the children be successful and develop their knowledge of the code more securely. Children also choose a book from our Infant Library to take home and share alongside their decodable text, to support their comprehension and foster their love of reading.
As pupils move through the Initial Code, they read books which are closely matched to their phonics knowledge. In this way, pupils are encouraged to use their phonics skills and knowledge as their primary reading strategy. Our expectation is that pupils should be reading with fluency before moving up to the next reading level. As pupils become efficient in decoding words quickly and independently, their reading increases as does the number of words they can read automatically. Increasing the pace of reading is an important objective in order to support developing reading comprehension. Pupils are encouraged to read aloud as well as silently. As pupils progress through the Extended Code, many begin reading longer texts with a greater number of complex words independently and with increasing fluency. This process culminates in a shift from learning to read to reading to learn where pupils progress to reading both for pleasure and for information.
Supporting Early Reading

The governing body meets once every half-term.
There are statutory committees which meet when required which are:-
Admissions Committee Headteacher’s Performance Management Review Panel Chair Pay Performance Review Panel
There are special positions on the Governing Body and these are filled
Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
and Safeguarding Governor – Georgina Knight Health & Safety Governor - Antoni Daszewski

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading | St. Peter's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reading
It is really important to read at home! Reading has the power to benefit your child in so many ways. It can improve your child's understanding and analysis of the world around them through questioning and exploration of a text and its pictures. Reading can help expand your child's imagination and inspire them to try ideas they may not have otherwise thought of. Crucially, the development of reading is very closely linked with their development in all other areas of learning, especially writing.
Parents can support their child's reading development by regularly reading at home. Just 10 minutes every evening can make a huge difference. Please see the Parent Guides below for additional guidance or speak to your class teacher.
Supporting KS1 and KS2 Reading at Home

Reading can help expand your child's imagination and inspire them to try ideas they may not have otherwise thought of. Crucially, the development of reading is very closely linked with their development in all other areas of learning, especially writing.
Parents can support their child's reading development by regularly reading at home. Just 10 minutes every evening can make a huge difference. Please see the Parent Guides below for additional guidance or speak to your class teacher.
